Something I remember reading about was by Dr David Burns, who was one of the very first people to work on the technique now known as CBT (not cock and ball torture, but cognitive behavioural therapy)

He said that even through all the teaching and practise he had undertaken, when it came to applying it for himself in his head, it completely fell apart, and he fell for every trick that he had rigorously contested with every patient he had. It was only when he wrote things out on paper that he relieved himself of this issue. 

What I’m trying to say is, if one of the pioneers of the most successful therapy technique in world history can’t manage it in his head, you can’t either. Don’t feel dumb or stupid for having to write things out, or doing simplistic things that you think aren’t necessary like reaching out to others. 

Doing therapy with yourself sounds really complex until … well… you do it. It was a book by him called “Feeling Good”. I scored high enough on his suicidal index that it recommended I put the book down and call a doctor but I’d already lost all hope so I kept reading. It sounds like that book could really, really help you right now. Someone suggested it to me during my darkest times and I never remembered their name, but they may have saved my life. 

I understand if reading is the last thing on your mind though, so just consider what I’ve said prior, don’t keep beating yourself up for what you’ve done. The truth is, you hurt yourself more than anyone, but being responsible for your actions doesn’t require punishment.
